#2972. Urban Outfitters (URBN) Q3 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 24, 2026 at 10:53PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Urban Outfitters (URBN +0.34%) reported record third quarter results with every brand contributing to 9% revenue growth and a 21% increase in earnings per share. Management noted the ninth consecutive quarter of record sales, highlighting the strength of the Free People Group and the continued scaling of the Nuuly subscription service. However, the company adopted a more cautious outlook for the fourth quarter and holiday season due to a dip in October store traffic and a slower-than-anticipated product transition at Anthropologie. While digital channels remain healthy, management anticipates higher promotional activity in the fourth quarter to clear legacy styles and address competitive holiday market dynamics.

Operator: Good day, ladies and gentlemen. And welcome to the Urban Outfitters Inc. Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Earnings Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press *11 on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press *11 again. We ask that you limit yourself to 1 question only. I would now like to introduce Oona McCullough, executive director of investor relations. Ma'am, you may begin.

Oona McCullough: Good afternoon. And welcome to the URBN Third Quarter Fiscal 27 Conference Call. Earlier this afternoon, the company issued a press release outlining the financial and operating results for the 3- and 9-month period ending October 31, 2026. The following discussions may include forward-looking statements. Please note that actual results may differ materially from those statements. Additional information concerning factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from projected results is contained in the company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. For more detailed commentary on our quarterly performance and the text of today's conference call, please refer to our Investor Relations website at www.urbn.com. I will now turn the call over to Dick.

Richard (Dick) A. Hayne: Thank you, Oona, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Our teams delivered another record quarter. With every brand contributing positively to our third quarter results. Q3 sales grew 9% to $1.7 billion, and earnings per share climbed 21% to $1.54 per share. This marks URBN's 9th consecutive quarter of record sales. All retail segment brands delivered positive comps once again demonstrating the strength of our brands and the consistency of our execution. The Free People Group produced standout results with record third quarter sales and operating profit. Urban Outfitters sustained positive comparable sales in both North America and Europe.

Alongside improved profitability. and the Anthropologie Group maintained positive comparable sales and double digit operating margins as their team continued to refine their product offering. Complementing the retail performance, both our wholesale and newly subscription segments delivered record third quarter revenues and operating profits. Looking ahead, our outlook for Q4 and the holiday season is a bit more cautious than when we last spoke in August. Total comp store traffic dipped into negative territory in October. Despite less traffic, higher average transaction values and solid conversion rates. Help keep overall comp store sales positive. But at a lower rate. Our digital business, however, remains strong. We anticipate higher promotions during the fourth quarter as Anthropologie works through its product transition.

That said, we feel confident our portfolio of strong brands and our multichannel model will continue to please our customers and drive long term value for our shareholders. Now Frank Conforti, our Co President and Chief Operating Officer, will discuss our third quarter performance in more detail after which our CFO, Melody Moran Efron will give our thoughts about the fourth quarter and year 2027. I will then wrap things up before opening the call for your questions. Frank?

Francis J. (Frank) Conforti: Thank you, Dick, and good afternoon, everyone. Today, I am excited to share our company's third quarter record results. Then I will dive into some detailed notes by brand, followed by an update regarding fuel costs. Overall, our teams delivered another outstanding quarter. Setting new sales and operating profit records. Total URBN sales grew by 9% reaching a Q3 record of $1.7 billion. All our retail segment brands delivered positive retail segment comps while 4 of our 5 brands posted record third quarter sales. Nuuly continued its impressive double digit revenue growth and our wholesale segment also delivered exceptional double digit revenue growth.

This expansion was driven by improvement in initial merchandise margins due in part to the year over year reduction of tariffs, which were only partially offset by higher inbound freight costs. Additionally, due to strong sales, we nicely leveraged the store occupancy expenses and through our ongoing initiatives, that improve customer service and lowered our cost per package we were able to continue leveraging delivery expenses. These benefits were partially offset by higher markdowns at the Anthropologie brand. Overall, through the team's strong execution, we were able to drive an improved gross profit margin rate despite the negative impacts of increased fuel costs. In the quarter, SG and A increased by 6% resulting in 64 basis points of leverage.

We are pleased to report that strong top line performance allowed us to continue investing in the business while also driving meaningful expense leverage. This leverage was primarily driven by strong sales which help us to successfully leverage store payroll expenses. As you will hear from Melanie, there is some timing in marketing spend that also benefited the third quarter. We are still planning on SG and A expenses being in line with sales for the full fiscal year. Overall, total URBN operating income grew by 19% compared to last year reaching a third quarter record operating income for URBN of $172 million.

Net income increased to $134 million while earnings per share increased by 21% to $1.54 per diluted share. Now moving on to brand performance, starting with Anthropologie. The Anthropologie brand reported total revenue growth of 3% driven by a 2% retail segment comp with positive results in digital and flat performance in stores. Results were driven by positive comps in women's apparel and accessories, while home was slightly negative for the quarter. Looking closer at Anthropologie's product performance, women's apparel delivered positive comps though the quarter played out a bit differently than we initially anticipated. Coming out of the second quarter, we were encouraged by early reads from our July fall event.

However, as the third quarter progressed, it proved more difficult than we anticipated to move through some of our legacy styles. While the new fashion deliveries are emerging as customer favorites, in several categories, others are taking longer to reach their full potential resulting in regular-price and overall sales to fall short of our plans in the third quarter. Accessories remained a bright spot. Delivering strong comp growth driven in part by continued strength in shoes. Meanwhile, home was slightly negative. While furniture delivered a positive comp, it was not enough to offset softness in home accessories. A category that has remained challenging all year and represents a higher penetration of our business in the third and fourth quarters.

Despite the pockets of product softness, Anthropologie's results reflect a well managed business that continues to deliver positive top line growth and a healthy double digit operating margin rate. Customer growth remains positive as the brand grew total customers by 3%, displaying well executed marketing campaigns and the overall underlying strength of the brand. As we look ahead to the fourth quarter, we are taking a slightly more measured view of the brand's near term trajectory. Moving through the remaining legacy product is requiring more time and deeper promotions than originally planned. And while our new product is resonating, the pace of adoption has been more gradual.

As a result, rather than seeing the markdown improvement we had previously anticipated against last year's elevated levels, we now believe fourth quarter markdowns at Anthropologie will be higher than the fourth quarter last year. We believe the brand is positioned to deliver flattish comps in the fourth quarter as the team continues to refine the assortment. Now turning to the Urban Outfitters brand. Total Urban Outfitters sales grew by 5% and the global retail segment comp was 6%. With strength across both North America and Europe. Store comps outperformed digital comps in both markets during the quarter.

In North America, the team delivered a 4% retail segment comp, This comp marks a healthy acceleration on a 2 year stack as the brand in North America was up against a 10% comp increase in the prior year third quarter. All categories except home delivered positive comps in the quarter. Strength in women's apparel continues to be driven by a strong bottoms trend, with outperformance coming from our own brands, including BDG, and IS Francis. BDG is truly evolving into a full lifestyle brand. Seeing great success expanding into sweaters, knits, and handbags, while BDG continues to deliver exceptional bottoms performance.

The brand continued to build momentum with its marketing initiatives, shifting a large portion of its social media strategy to video, and leaning heavily into user generated content. By deploying these assets across the right channels, the team is effectively meeting customers where they are. Expanding their reach on platforms like TikTok, Reddit, and ChatGPT while continuing to partner with DoorDash on unique customer activations. Building on the success of their first ever back to school connected TV campaign, the brand launched its the more the merrier, holiday campaign to carry that momentum into the fourth quarter. In Europe, the business has remained consistently strong. Even against increasingly impressive multiyear comparisons. Delivering its 9th consecutive quarter of positive comps.

The European team produced an 8% retail segment comp this quarter, with stores outperforming the digital channel. This performance was driven by positive comps in all major categories with strong results in women's accessories, and apparel. Through compelling product assortments, and highly engaging marketing campaigns across multiple platforms and customer experiences, the brand continues to capture meaningful market share in the region. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we believe the global Urban Outfitters retail segment comp could be in the mid single digit positive range with both North America and Europe delivering mid single digit positive comps.

Overall, the total brand has delivered 9 consecutive quarters of improved profitability, and we still believe Urban Outfitters can deliver a low single-digit operating profit rate for the full year even when factoring in the headwinds from higher freight and delivery expenses driven by increased fuel surcharges. Next, let's turn to the FP group. The FP Group delivered another impressive performance this quarter. Achieving a total revenue increase of 15%. This growth was driven by positive retail segment comps, new store growth, and strong gains in the wholesale segment. The retail segment comp of 9% was broad based across both the store and digital channels. With store performance outpacing digital during the quarter.

Customer traffic and AUR were nicely positive across both channels and positive comps were driven by strong regular price sales. Reflecting the high quality of the brand's offering and strong customer demand. Meanwhile, The FP Group's Wholesale segment delivered a 21% increase in revenue during the quarter. Led by continued strength in FB movement, apparel, accessories, and intimates across our wholesale partners. This execution, combined with disciplined inventory management, enabled the FP Group to deliver record operating profit dollars for the third quarter. Within the FP Group, the Free People brand had a strong third quarter. Delivering total revenue growth of 11% and a retail segment comp of 7%. These positive comps were driven by continued strength in key categories.

Led by bottoms, accessories, and intimates. The FP Movement brand, also remained a standout. Delivering exceptional results with total revenue growth of 27% and a 12% retail segment comp. Both brands executed highly effective marketing campaigns during the quarter. That showcased their creativity and built deeper brand awareness. At Free People, the team launched a clever take on celebrating product innovation titled jacket too good to take off. Which featured a live coat check girl activation in a New York City store window that drove significant awareness across social platforms. The team also launched a campaign with musician and actress Willow Smith. Highlighting a true brand fan while celebrating her creativity.

Meanwhile, FP Movement created meaningful community moments by partnering with DICK'S Sporting Goods for the Move With Us tour. Celebrating women owned studios as well as collaborating with the Montauk General Store on an in store pop up event. Both initiatives deepened FP Movements connection with its target customer. Finally, we also want to highlight the continued strength of the brand's international business. While still a relatively small portion of the overall brand, international is steadily building awareness and traction. With 16 stores currently open and delivering an impressive 19% retail segment comp in the quarter. Looking ahead, the FB Group continues to carry strong momentum into the holiday season.

We remain committed to growing Nuuly toward its significant long term revenue potential while continuing to improve its profitability. The last topic I want to briefly touch upon is the overall transportation cost environment and its impact on our business. As we have discussed previously, we are currently navigating higher inbound freight costs domestic transportation costs, and higher delivery expenses driven by fuel surcharges associated with the ongoing war in the Middle East. These additional costs had a negative impact of approximately 55 basis points in IMU, and approximately 20 basis points in outbound delivery and freight expense. We are assuming these costs and their negative margin impact will remain consistent for the remainder of the year.

As noted earlier, through the team's disciplined execution, we were able to more than offset these macro headwinds and deliver increases in gross profit margin dollars and rate in the quarter. If the price of fuel declines and stabilizes, at any point in time in the future, we would expect to see a corresponding reduction in these expenses. In closing, our third quarter results reflect the underlying strength of our diversified portfolio. Delivering 9% total revenue growth positive comps across all of our retail brands, double digit subscription and wholesale segment growth, driving a 21% increase in our earnings per share.

As we enter the holiday season, our teams remain focused on delivering compelling products and engaging customer experiences across every brand. I will now turn the call over to Melanie Marein-Efron, our Chief Financial Officer, to share our outlook for the fourth quarter.

Based on the current sales performance and plans, we believe our fourth quarter gross profit margins could improve by approximately 25 basis points versus last year. The increase in Q4 gross profit rate could be primarily due to higher IMU due in part to lower tariffs versus last year, and occupancy leverage partially offset by higher fuel surcharges, higher markdowns at the Anthropologie Group, and increased labor and fulfillment costs versus last year. We are assuming that current oil surcharges related to the ongoing Middle East war to remain in effect for the remainder of fiscal year 27. These surcharges, which began in March 2026, impact inbound freight and outbound delivery and freight expenses.

And we estimate they will have an approximate 75-basis-point unfavorable impact on the fourth quarter gross margin. Based on our current plans, we believe our full year fiscal 27 adjusted gross profit margins could improve versus last year despite the fuel surcharges which we have experienced for much of the fiscal year. Based on our current sales performance and financial plan, we believe that total growth in SG and A could outpace sales growth in Q4. The growth in SG and A dollars are based on planned marketing investments at all brands to support new customer acquisition along with increased store payroll costs related to sales growth.

In Q4, SG and A could grow at a rate slightly ahead of sales due to the timing of marketing investments. For the full year, we believe that SG and A could grow at a rate in line with sales growth. As always, if sales performance fluctuates, we maintain a certain level of variable SG and A spending that we can fluctuate up and down depending on how our business is performing. We are planning for an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 25.5% for the fourth quarter and 24.1% for the full year. The increases versus last year are primarily attributable to the ratio of foreign taxable earnings to global taxable earnings.

Now moving on to inventory, We continue to be focused on increasing our inventory productivity and product turns. We believe that our inventory levels could grow at a rate at or below sales growth in Q4. For fiscal year 27, capital expenditures are planned at $475 million The capital project spend is broken down as follows. Approximately 30% for retail store expansion and support, approximately 55% for logistics investments, and the remaining 15% for technology investments and home office expansion, support our growing businesses. The logistics investments are to expand our capacity and automation in both the subscription and retail segment businesses. We will be opening approximately 47 new stores and closing approximately 14 stores during fiscal year 27.

Our net new store growth is primarily being driven by growth in FP Group stores, During FY 27, we plan on opening 17 FP Movement stores. 11 Free People brand stores, 10 Anthropologie Group stores, and 8 Urban Outfitters stores. As a reminder, the foregoing does not constitute a forecast but is simply a reflection of our current views. The company disclaims any obligation to update forward-looking statements. Now it is my pleasure to turn the call back to Dick Hayne, chief executive officer of URBN.

I want to recognize the hard work our brand and shared service leaders, their teams, and our co presidents, Meg and Frank. I deeply appreciate the commitment and talent you bring to making our brands resonate with our customers. I also thank our global partners for their continued collaboration and our shareholders for their ongoing support. That concludes our prepared remarks. As a reminder, please limit your questions to 1 per caller. We now invite your questions.

TL;DR: Surging tech stocks aren't great news for bonds, or for mortgage rates.

Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points higher than yesterday and four basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Recently news about big tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

Today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

Here's the thing, though: Markets are fickle. They also move fast. And they aren't the only influence on mortgage rates.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Lately, we've seen two narratives influencing mortgage rates battling it out; depending on which one's stronger, daily rates move higher or lower. Up top I talked about how shifting perceptions of big tech have been driving mortgage rates (and yes, today, pushing them higher, though usually it's pulled rates down.) When rates are moving higher, more often it's been thanks to inflation — and while it's a lightweight work week, we're about to get heavyweight inflation news.

The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely.

The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

Predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

And speaking of: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

P.S.: I don't have to ask if anyone's playing Grand Theft Auto 'cause c'mon, of course. But did anyone else perk up when Lu asked about home loans? Yeah, that was probably just me. Jason and Lucia would have to change a lot about their lifestyle to qualify (we know they're working on building credit, but having all your income be cash you can't really document is not going to work for a lender). But hey, I'm rooting for them.

» Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

The rate you see advertised is a sample rate — usually for a borrower with perfect credit, making a big down payment, and paying for mortgage points. That won't match every buyer's circumstances.

In addition to market factors outside of your control, your customized quote depends on your:

Even two people with similar credit scores might get different rates, depending on their overall financial profiles.

#2968. Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney

#2966. I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

“Buy now, pay later” can help stretch your holiday budget further, but pick your BNPL app carefully and avoid loan stacking.

Head of Content, Personal & Student Loans

As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

It’s a big list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) plan to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL users expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

Brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, says many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

“They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”

Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

While Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how important it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison says BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

“With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he says.

Not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

There are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

Long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

Pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

Harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL company doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

Because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

According to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL users had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison says.

“If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he says. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”

Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

Still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison says, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

“Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he says. “There's a big difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”

#2964. Anthropic vs. SpaceX: Here's the Better IPO Stock to Buy With $1,000 Right Now

While Anthropic is growing at an extraordinary pace, Space Exploration Technologies offers investors a more diversified way to capitalize on the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution.

By Adam Spatacco – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:15PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›

Two of the most highly anticipated initial public offerings (IPOs) in Wall Street history took place this year. Following the public debut of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -5.65%) in June, artificial intelligence (AI) developer Anthropic (ANT -6.54%) listed on the Nasdaq just last week.

While both companies are capitalizing on insatiable demand for AI, their respective business models are considerably different. Interestingly, the relationship between Anthropic and SpaceX is much deeper than most investors realize.

Let's explore the investment thesis for each company and assess which AI stock represents the more compelling opportunity for investors with $1,000 to deploy right now.

Anthropic's Claude family of large language models (LLMs) has emerged as a leading platform across software development, enterprise productivity, and agentic AI. The company's ability to integrate its technology into Fortune 500 workflows presents an enormous opportunity to capture enterprise software spending across the market.

During the third quarter, Anthropic generated roughly $17 billion in revenue, representing a jaw-dropping 1,127% year-over-year increase. By the end of October, the company's annualized revenue run rate had reached nearly $81 billion.

Despite this impressive top-line growth, the rest of Anthropic's financial profile raises some concerns. During the third quarter alone, the company incurred $9.9 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses while recording an operating loss of $567 million.

Perhaps most concerning is that Anthropic has $901 billion in infrastructure commitments. Although these obligations span several years, they illustrate the enormous financial resources required to remain competitive in frontier AI development.

Anthropic also faces competition from OpenAI's ChatGPT, Alphabet's Gemini, SpaceX's Grok, and an expanding ecosystem of open-weight models. As competing models become more sophisticated, Anthropic will likely face pricing pressure at exactly the time it needs to generate returns on its infrastructure investments.

While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets and Starlink satellite internet service, the company's AI infrastructure business is swiftly becoming its largest growth engine.

During the third quarter, SpaceX generated $14.6 billion in total revenue, up 161% year over year and 87% sequentially. Unlike Anthropic, SpaceX also generated positive operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion.

The table illustrates how SpaceX's revenue growth is unfolding across its three business segments.

Management expects SpaceX to reach a $100 billion annualized revenue run rate by December, driven in large part by accelerating demand for AI infrastructure. Interestingly, one of the biggest catalysts behind this milestone is none other than Anthropic.

Earlier this year, SpaceX disclosed that Anthropic had agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month for access to its Colossus 1 data center. This gave Anthropic access to more than 300 megawatts of new capacity, powered by more than 220,000 Nvidia GPUs.

However, Anthropic's S-1 filing revealed that the relationship with SpaceX expanded substantially. Anthropic may spend up to $120.5 billion on SpaceX's compute services through 2029. Once all contracted capacity is delivered, monthly payments could reach $3.1 billion. This equates to $37.2 billion in annualized revenue and nearly 2.5x the original monthly arrangement.

Of course, SpaceX isn't immune to risk. The company also faces substantial infrastructure expenditures and must compete with hyperscalers and specialized AI cloud providers. Moreover, there is uncertainty surrounding the company's ambitions to build orbital data centers.

In addition, Anthropic's computing agreements contain termination provisions. This means investors should not treat the entire $120.5 billion as guaranteed revenue.

The biggest difference between Anthropic and SpaceX is that Elon Musk's space empire offers investors more diversified exposure to technological innovation. Anthropic's success largely hinges on its ability to monetize AI models profitably. By contrast, SpaceX can capitalize on demand for AI infrastructure alongside satellite connectivity, commercial space exploration, government contracting, and its own AI software.

This distinction is important when considering how quickly the AI landscape is evolving. SpaceX doesn't necessarily need Grok to defeat Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini to build a lucrative AI business. The company can simply monetize demand for compute from competing AI developers, regardless of which platform emerges as the market leader.

Admittedly, both SpaceX and Anthropic command premium valuations. Nevertheless, SpaceX's combination of established businesses, emerging market opportunities, and improving profitability provides a more compelling foundation for long-term investors.

Rather than betting $1,000 on a particular AI model developer like Anthropic, I'd prefer to allocate that capital to SpaceX and gain exposure to several transformative markets all at once. Ironically, investing in SpaceX could prove to be one of the more attractive ways to capitalize on Anthropic's future success.

#2962. Etihad’s New Credit Cards Are Primarily for Status Chasers

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

The new cards offer perks like faster paths to status and elevated earning rates when purchasing tickets with partners.

Etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two new credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for new applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

The earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

Those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.)

One of the most interesting perks of the new cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

You want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s important to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:

Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card

No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card

Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card

Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®

Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®

#2960. What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Used-car dealers may charge you a reconditioning fee to cover their costs of getting cars ready for sale.

A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

Service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

Detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several users suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

#2956. What Are Repositioning Cruises?

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Repositioning cruises move ships between seasonal destinations, often with longer sailings, fewer port stops and lower fares.

A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

One key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy shows, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

This journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between New York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and New England before reaching the Big Apple.

Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching New York.

#2955. The Semiconductor ETF Kept Falling After Nvidia Raised Its Forecast. Time to Buy?

The chip fund kept falling after its top holding raised its sales forecast.

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:37PM EST

10 stocks we like better than VanEck ETF Trust - VanEck Semiconductor ETF ›

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH -7.26%) slid about 7% on Tuesday, Nov. 24, while chip shares fell broadly. The fund traded near $420 as I write, off about 37% from its June 22 record close of $668.91.

It's still up about 19% for 2026, after finishing last year at $360.13. But most of this year's rise is gone.

In mid-November, I wrote that the fund was a buy at around $500. It's about 15% cheaper now. And I think the fund's top holding has given investors more reason to buy since then.

Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) made up around 18.5% of the fund's assets on Nov. 23, almost double the weight of any other stock. This makes the company's Nov. 17 earnings report the biggest news for the fund in weeks.

The results were strong. Nvidia's revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, the three months ending Oct. 25, hit $115.8 billion, up 103% from $57.0 billion a year ago. It also grew 20% from the $96.2 billion Nvidia took in during fiscal Q2. Non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share rose 111% year over year. For the current quarter, which has an extra week, Nvidia expects around $130 billion in revenue.

Management also raised its outlook for fiscal 2028, a year that roughly matches calendar 2027. It now expects revenue to grow around 75% that year, up from the 70% it predicted earlier, and from a bigger fiscal 2027 total.

"[W]ith demand far exceeding supply, we expect our performance to remain strong," Colette Kress, then Nvidia's interim CEO and chief financial officer, said on the earnings call.

Nvidia's leadership has been less stable. The company said on Nov. 12 that co-founder Jensen Huang had stepped down as CEO, and on Nov. 23 that its board had reinstated him. The fund surged around 15% that day.

But the fund's dropped about 7% since Nvidia's results. The biggest part of the fund, then, has a stronger outlook than a week ago, at a lower price.

At roughly $151 a share on Tuesday, Nvidia trades at about 9 times earnings, using the average analyst forecast for its fiscal 2028.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -3.96%), the fund's No. 2 holding at almost 10% of its assets, costs about 15 times the earnings analysts expect from it in 2027. And its sales are speeding up. The company's October revenue grew about 60% year over year, faster than its 43% gain for the first 10 months of 2026.

Broadcom, about 6% of the fund, costs roughly 16 times its estimated fiscal 2027 earnings. By comparison, FactSet had the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.50%) at about 17 times the earnings expected for the next 12 months in its Nov. 20 report.

Not all holdings are as cheap. Texas Instruments and Advanced Micro Devices, each about 5% to 6% of the fund, trade at roughly 22 or 23 times their estimated 2027 earnings.

But the stocks with the most weight in the fund look priced as if their profits are near a peak. I think that view is too pessimistic, especially for Nvidia after it raised its forecast.

They could. Chip profits can shrink fast when demand slows or supply catches up. In Nvidia's fiscal 2023, which ended in January 2023, its adjusted earnings per share fell 25%.

But a drop that big wouldn't make the stock look expensive at today's price. If Nvidia's fiscal 2028 earnings landed 25% under what analysts forecast, its current price would be around 12 times earnings, still far below the S&P 500's level of about 17 times expected earnings.

The fund won't even out the swings, either. It closed Nov. 20 at $400.06, surged the next session, then dropped about as much as Nvidia did on Tuesday. Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor together make up over a quarter of the fund's assets, and its 10 biggest holdings about 69%.

Owning the fund does mean an investor doesn't need to guess which chipmaker will be next to face news like Nvidia's CEO change.

At roughly $420, I'd buy the fund and plan to hold it for years. The stocks that make up most of it are priced modestly against the profits expected next year, and the largest of them is one of the cheapest.

I'd think again if Nvidia lowered its forecast of about 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.

#2954. Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters."

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth."

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates are down this morning, but could seesaw back up tomorrow.

Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

The amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.)

My point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

Strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

Predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Markets are currently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

But back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

» Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.
